notes.Nikola Jokic: Denver opens its season tonight at Oklahoma City in a 236.5-point game, tied for the highest total on the slate. The Thunder are 9.5-point favorites, so a blowout is the one thing that could cap his minutes.
notes.Shai Gilgeous-Alexander: He scored 32 points in 36 minutes in the opener against San Antonio, and he and Jared McCain carried the offense when the Spurs made their second-half run.
notes.Donovan Mitchell: Cleveland opens tonight at Philadelphia in a 236.5-point game, and Jarrett Allen is questionable with a knee issue, which would put even more of the offense on Mitchell and James Harden.
notes.Tyrese Maxey: He played 40 minutes and scored 28 points in the opener against the Knicks, the heaviest workload on the team.
notes.Jaylon Tyson: He is Cleveland's sixth man, can play the one through the three and crashes the offensive glass. If Jarrett Allen (questionable, knee) sits, Mobley slides to center and more wing minutes open up for him.
notes.Cameron Johnson: He starts at forward for Denver, and Julian Strawther's knee sprain takes a wing out of the rotation for at least six weeks.
notes.Sam Merrill: He should play every night in Cleveland's rotation, and if Jarrett Allen (questionable) sits, the shift of Mobley to center opens more wing minutes for him.
notes.Anfernee Simons: He played 25 minutes off the bench in the opener and hit three 3-pointers as the Sixers' reserves found open looks.
notes.Cason Wallace: He started the opener but played only 19 minutes, with Alex Caruso, Ajay Mitchell and Jared McCain all playing more off the bench.
notes.Jared McCain: He hit 6 of 8 threes for 20 points in 22 minutes off the bench in the opener.
notes.Alex Caruso: He played 25 minutes off the bench in the opener, more than starter Cason Wallace, and his minutes tend to climb against strong teams like Denver.
notes.Tyus Jones: He is Denver's backup point guard behind Jamal Murray in a thin Nuggets rotation.
